poems:
7:00. The toaster clicks down like a small guillotine.
Upstairs, somebody is losing an argument with a sock.
Milk poured to the exact line of the bowl's blue stripe, then past it.

Lunch:
turkey, no crust.
apple, uneaten, returning.
juice box, hostage.
napkin, optimistic.
The dog has decided this is the important part of the day and stands directly in it.
This kitchen runs on the stove hood and stubbornness.

Shoes:
one by the door,
one under the couch,
the third theory unexplored.

A violin case by the door,
resented daily.
7:07. Nobody has said anything true yet.

Fill the pot to the second line.
Press the button already pressed.
Wait for the noise
that makes the day legal.
The bus makes its sound two streets over and everyone converts to a different religion.
7:10 is the last minute anything can be found.
A banana on the counter, one brown shoulder.
In the car already. Engine off, radio on, a small private country.
The podcast host is very excited about a company you will never hear of again.
Hair wet at the ends, collar damp, out the door anyway.
7:15. The negotiation over the second waffle enters its diplomatic phase.

Through the wall:
fine. FINE.
Both meant.
A crossing guard adjusts her vest and takes the corner like it belongs to her.
Somebody's grandmother has been dressed for an hour, with nowhere in particular to be.

Toast crumbs on the black shirt.
One swipe.
Two.
Good enough.
7:20. Whatever wasn't packed is not coming.
The bathroom door, closed, and the small parliament forming outside it.

Vitamin.
Pill.
Second pill.
The glass of water that makes it a ceremony.

Receipt, gas station, 7:23 a.m.:
large coffee, one banana, lottery ticket.
Hope in three denominations.
A man in a truck eats a sandwich with both hands and steers with a knee.

7:25. Shoes tied by an adult,
on a child, at speed.

front-door checklist, n.
The four things you touch,
and the fifth you remember
at the second stoplight.
The kid has questions about death. The kid has three minutes.
Cold pizza, eaten standing, held like evidence.
Nurses in the elevator, coats still on, saying almost nothing.

7:30. The permission slip surfaces,
due today, signed on the dryer.
A hairbrush will turn up in the freezer on Saturday and explain some of this.

The neighbor's car, started from the kitchen,
idles in the driveway with nobody in it, proving something.
Yesterday's mug in the sink, the ring already set like small geology.
You will remember it at 9:40, in a meeting, and it will keep.
7:35. An alarm goes off for the fourth time and this one is real.

7:36. The tie rack offers forty options
and one answer.
The office is already lit for people who are not in it.

7:38. One shoe is in the house.
The house denies it.
Bus 44 pulls out with eleven people and one bicycle.
7:40 here. Lunch somewhere. Somewhere else, a bar floor getting mopped.
The email you sent last night looks worse now.
Sprinkler heads on grass nobody walks on.
Did you feed the fish, asked in a tone that already knows.
Somebody puts on a name tag in a parking lot, using the side mirror.
7:45. The front door opens and shuts four times in ninety seconds.

Missing:
one library book, blue,
due since March.
Reward: peace.

7:47. The thermostat, adjusted,
readjusted by a different hand.
A jogger passes the same trash can she passed yesterday. Neither acknowledges it.
Hands under the tap too long, watching nothing.
7:50. Whoever is still home has decided to be late and is enjoying it.
Second load of laundry, started by somebody who will not be here to move it.
A whistle. Two short. Everyone obeys a stranger.
Coffee gone cold in the cupholder, which was always going to happen.
A row of paper cups on a counter, each with a name spelled adventurously.
The last one out never checks the stove. The first one back always does.
Somebody sits down in a parked car and does not turn the key for a while.
On the radio, a voice reads the backups on the interstate with real tenderness.
The cat takes the warm spot on the bed the second it comes available.
7:59. The house, briefly, belongs to nobody.
